title: Finite-order differential operators extend to prime localizations
statement: Let $R\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, let $\mathfrak p\subset B$ be a prime ideal, and write $j:B\to B_{\mathfrak p}$ for the ordinary localization map [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. For any commutative $R$-algebra $C$, an $R$-linear map $D:C\to C$ has differential order at most $0$ if it is $C$-linear; recursively, it has differential order at most $r>0$ if, for every $c\in C$, the $R$-linear map $[D,c]:x\mapsto D(cx)-cD(x)$ has differential order at most $r-1$. Let $r\ge0$ and let $D:B\to B$ be $R$-linear of differential order at most $r$. There exists a unique $R$-linear map $\widetilde D:B_{\mathfrak p}\to B_{\mathfrak p}$ of differential order at most $r$ such that $\widetilde D(j(b))=j(D(b))$ for every $b\in B$.

source.place: Tag 0G36, lemma-invert-system-differential-operators, specialized to M=N=B and the multiplicative set B minus p; differential order is Definition 09CI, definition-differential-operators.

proof.text: Put $S=B\setminus\mathfrak p$ and $A=B_{\mathfrak p}$. By [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], elements of $A$ are fractions $b/s$, and $b/s=c/t$ means $u(tb-sc)=0$ for some $u\in S$. Write $\mu_a$ for multiplication by $a$ on whichever ring is under consideration. Induct on the bound $r$, proving existence and uniqueness together for every operator on $B$. For $r=0$, $D(b)=bD(1)$, so multiplication by $j(D(1))$ is the required extension; every $A$-linear endomorphism of $A$ is determined by its value at $1$, proving uniqueness.

The zero map, sums and differences of operators of order at most $n$ again have order at most $n$: induct on $n$, using linearity at $n=0$ and $[T+U,c]=[T,c]+[U,c]$, $[-T,c]=-[T,c]$ for the induction step. Multiplication maps have order $0$. Thus [lem-trf-differential-operator-composition-order], with one bound equal to $0$, shows that precomposing or postcomposing an order-at-most-$n$ operator with multiplication by any element preserves its bound. These assertions apply both over $B/R$ and over $A/R$.

source.place: Tags 09CI and 09CJ, closure under sums and composition with order-zero maps

proof.text:
Assume $r>0$ and the assertion for bound $r-1$. For $b\in B$, put $L_b=[D,b]$, and let $E_b:A\to A$ be its unique extension of order at most $r-1$ given by induction. Expansion on an element of $B$ gives $L_{bc}=L_b\mu_c+\mu_bL_c$ and $[L_b,c]=[L_c,b]$. Every corresponding sum or commutator of the $E_b$ has order at most $r-1$ by Step 2 and [lem-trf-differential-operator-composition-order]. Uniqueness in the induction hypothesis therefore gives
$$E_{bc}=E_b\mu_{j(c)}+\mu_{j(b)}E_c,\qquad [E_b,j(c)]=[E_c,j(b)].$$
Both sides restrict along $j$ to the same displayed operator on $B$. In particular $E_1=0$, since $L_1=0$.

Define a proposed value on a fraction $z=b/s$ by
$$E(z)=j(s)^{-1}\bigl(j(D(b))-E_s(z)\bigr).$$
For $t\in S$, the refined representative $tb/(ts)$ gives the same value: Step 3 yields $E_{ts}(z)=E_t(j(b))+j(t)E_s(z)=j(L_t(b))+j(t)E_s(z)$, whereas $j(D(tb))=j(t)j(D(b))+j(L_t(b))$. Subtraction and division by $j(ts)$ give exactly the original value. If $b/s=c/t$, choose $u\in S$ with $u(tb-sc)=0$ using [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Refining the first representative by $ut$ and the second by $us$ gives equal numerators $utb=usc$ and equal denominators $uts=ust$. Refinement invariance therefore proves well-definedness even when $j$ has a kernel.

For fractions with a fixed denominator $s$, the formula in Step 4 is additive in the numerator and commutes with multiplication by an element of $R$, since $D$ and $E_s$ are $R$-linear. Any two fractions have a common denominator $st$, so refinement invariance proves additivity on all of $A$; the same formula proves $R$-linearity. For $s=1$, $E_1=0$, so $E(j(b))=j(D(b))$ for every $b\in B$.

For $b,c\in B$, $s\in S$, and $z=c/s$, the defining formula gives
$$j(s)\bigl(E(j(b)z)-j(b)E(z)\bigr)=j(L_b(c))-[E_s,j(b)](z).$$
The second identity of Step 3 replaces the last commutator by $[E_b,j(s)]$. Since $E_b(j(c))=j(L_b(c))$ and $j(s)z=j(c)$, the right side is $j(s)E_b(z)$. Multiplication by the unit $j(s)$ is injective, hence $[E,j(b)]=E_b$. In the endomorphism ring of the $R$-module $A$, multiplying out also gives
$$[E,j(s)^{-1}]=-\mu_{j(s)^{-1}}[E,j(s)]\mu_{j(s)^{-1}}=-\mu_{j(s)^{-1}}E_s\mu_{j(s)^{-1}}.$$
By [lem-trf-differential-operator-composition-order] and Step 2, all these commutators have order at most $r-1$.

Here is the algebra-generator test used in Tag 0G35, written out in this instance. Let $H$ be the set of $a\in A$ for which $[E,a]$ has order at most $r-1$. It contains the image of $R$, since $E$ is $R$-linear and its commutator with such a scalar is zero. It is closed under addition and negation by Step 2 and $[E,a+a']=[E,a]+[E,a']$. It is closed under products because
$$[E,aa']=[E,a]\mu_{a'}+\mu_a[E,a'],$$
and composing with the order-zero multiplication maps preserves order by [lem-trf-differential-operator-composition-order]. Thus $H$ is an $R$-subalgebra. Step 6 puts every $j(b)$ and $j(s)^{-1}$ in $H$. Every fraction is $j(b)j(s)^{-1}$, so $H=A$. By the recursive definition, $E$ has order at most $r$.

source.place: Tag 0G35, lemma-check-differential-operators, its subalgebra proof; Tag 09CJ, lemma-composition-differential-operators

proof.text:
Finally let $F:A\to A$ be any extension of $D$ of order at most $r$. For each $s\in S$, the commutator $[F,j(s)]$ has order at most $r-1$ and restricts along $j$ to $L_s$. The uniqueness part of the induction hypothesis gives $[F,j(s)]=E_s$. Evaluating at $z=b/s$ yields
$$j(D(b))=F(j(s)z)=j(s)F(z)+E_s(z),$$
so $F(z)=j(s)^{-1}(j(D(b))-E_s(z))=E(z)$. All fractions occur in this way; hence $F=E$. This completes the induction and proves the stated existence, bound, and uniqueness.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0G36, lemma-invert-system-differential-operators, specialized to M=N=B; Tag 0G35 generator test expanded and omitted uniqueness supplied in Step 8.
